newsitem.title: DUBAI: Banbar Abbas refinery to run Iran Heavy crude.
newsitem.headline: Banbar Abbas refinery to run Iran Heavy crude.

text.p: Iran's new Bandar Abbas oil refinery will process 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iranian Heavy crude and 12,000 bpd of Sarkhoon gas condensate when fully operational, the Tehran Times newspaper reported on Thursday.
"Precommissioning and commissioning of the refinery started in March 1997 and already some of the units are on stream, producing marketable products," Tehran Times reported.

The $2 billion Bandar Abbas plant, Iran's eighth refinery, is expected to start post-commissioning operations in July and reach full capacity in September, according to comments made by Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh at June's OPEC meeting.
The plant will be an export-orientated refinery but will also supply middle distillates to the growing domestic market.

Bandar Abbas director Ibrahim Zamanzadeh was quoted this month as saying that Iran would not need to import gasoline, kerosene and diesel fuel after March 1998 when the plant's two distillation units would be running at full capacity.
